question: Which heart chamber has the thickest muscular wall to pump blood?
explanation: The left ventricle needs a thicker wall because it must generate enough pressure to pump blood through the entire systemic circulation. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T4#GNS111_U2_T4_h1)

question: The primary function of heart valves is to ensure blood flows in what direction?
explanation: Valves act as one-way gates that open to let blood pass forward and snap shut to prevent it from flowing backward. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T4#GNS111_U2_T4_h1)

question: The right side of the heart pumps deoxygenated blood to which organ?
explanation: Deoxygenated blood travels from the right ventricle through the pulmonary artery to the lungs for gaseous exchange. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T4#GNS111_U2_T4_h2)

question: What triggers the release of Atrial Natriuretic Peptide from the heart?
explanation: When blood volume rises, the walls of the atria stretch, prompting them to release ANP to help reduce blood volume and pressure. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T4#GNS111_U2_T4_h2)

question: Which structure is known as the primary pacemaker of the heart?
explanation: The sinoatrial node sets the normal pace of the heart by firing impulses faster than any other part of the conduction system. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T4#GNS111_U2_T4_h3)

question: Why does the electrical impulse pause briefly at the AV node?

options.A: To reverse the direction of blood flow
options.B: To let the SA node rest and recharge
options.C: To prevent the heart from beating too fast
options.D: To allow ventricles to fill with blood

explanation: The short delay at the AV node ensures the atria finish contracting and empty their blood into the ventricles before ventricular contraction begins. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T4#GNS111_U2_T4_h3)

question: What physical event produces the first heart sound, known as 'lub'?

options.C: Filling of the atria with blood

explanation: The closure of the tricuspid and mitral valves at the start of ventricular systole causes the first heart sound. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T4#GNS111_U2_T4_h4)

question: During which phase of the cardiac cycle do the ventricles actively pump blood out?
explanation: Systole refers to contraction, so ventricular systole is the period when the ventricles contract to eject blood into the major arteries. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T4#GNS111_U2_T4_h4)

question: What does the P wave on an ECG tracing represent?
explanation: The P wave shows the electrical depolarization moving through the atria right before atrial contraction occurs. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T4#GNS111_U2_T4_h5)

question: Why is the QRS complex much larger in amplitude than the P wave?

options.A: Atria do not use electricity to contract
options.B: Ventricles contain much more muscle mass than atria
options.C: The electrical signal travels faster through ventricles
options.D: Electrodes are placed closer to the ventricles

explanation: The size of the wave on an ECG corresponds to the amount of tissue undergoing electrical change; ventricles are much larger and muscular than atria. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T4#GNS111_U2_T4_h5)
